full_judgment: 5. Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Ltd. which was incorporated in 1964 under the Companies Act, 1913, subsequently passed through different processes changing its status from a limited company to a public enterprise. In 1968 all of its shares held by the EPIDC were transferred to the President of Pakistan. After she emergence of Bangladesh, all of its shares became abandoned and vested in the Government of Bangladesh under the provisions of President's Order No. 16 of 1972. With she passing of President's Order No. 27 of 1972. ten corporations were created, one of them being the Bangladesh Minerals, oil and Gas Corporation. Subsequently, the Government of Bangladesh acquired exclusive right of exploitation and marketing of natural gas in Bangladesh under the provisions of the Petroleum Act, 1974. This Act has been passed in pursuance of Article 143 of the Constitution. Under the provisions of the aforesaid Act Bangladesh Mineral, Oil and Gas Corporation was re-constituted and became known as Pertro Bangla. The appellant's claim is that though ho has been placed by the Corporation as an employee of the enterprise and draws his salaries from it he is, in fact, an officer of the Corporation. In short, he enjoys the status of an employee of a statutory body.
